title: 是 — to be (A 是 B)
explanation: 是 (shì) links a subject to a noun to say what someone or something is. It is NOT used before an adjective — for adjectives use 很 (see the 很 lesson). Negate with 不是.
syllabus_ref: 句型·特殊句型「是」字句1（表示等同或类属）

title: 有 — to have / there is
explanation: 有 (yǒu) means 'to have' or 'there is/are'. Its negative is 没有 (méiyǒu) — never 不有.
syllabus_ref: 句型·特殊句型「有」字句1（表示领有）

examples.pinyin: wǒ yǒu yī gè mèi mei 。
jiā lǐ yǒu yī zhī māo 。
examples.en: There is a cat at home.

examples.pinyin: nǐ yǒu méi yǒu wèn tí ？

title: 很 — adjectives (no 是)
explanation: A Chinese adjective is a complete predicate, so you do NOT add 是 before it. 很 (hěn) 'very' is the default link; 非常 'extremely' and 太…了 'too…' are stronger.
syllabus_ref: 副词·程度副词：很、非常、太、真

title: 吗 — yes/no questions
explanation: Add 吗 (ma) to the end of a statement to make a yes/no question. The word order does not change.

title: Question words (什么 / 谁 / 哪儿 …)
pattern: replace the unknown with a question word
explanation: For a specific question, put a question word where the answer would go; the word order stays the same. 什么 what, 谁 who, 哪儿 where, 几/多少 how many.
syllabus_ref: 句类·疑问句（2）特指问句；代词·疑问代词

examples.pinyin: nǐ jiào shén me míng zi ？

title: 的 — 's / linking
explanation: 的 (de) shows possession (like 's) and links a modifier to a noun. Between close relations it is often dropped: 我妈妈.
syllabus_ref: 短语·「的」字短语；句子成分·定语

title: 了 — completed action / change
explanation: 了 after a verb marks a completed action (not past tense — it marks completion). 了 at the end of a sentence can mark a new situation / change of state.
syllabus_ref: 动作的态·完成态「了1」；变化态「了2」

examples.pinyin: tā mǎi le yī jiàn yī fu 。
examples.en: He bought a piece of clothing.

title: 想 / 要 / 会 / 能 — modal verbs
explanation: Modal verbs go before the main verb. 想 want to, 要 want / be going to, 会 can (learned skill) / will, 能 can (be able to), 可以 may.
syllabus_ref: 动词·能愿动词：会、能、想、要、可以
